name: Operating Systems & Systems Security
description: Kernel and OS-level security, isolation, sandboxing, virtualization, and access control.
narrative:
The earliest papers here, from 2018, were dominated by a single seismic event: the discovery that the hardware itself broke the memory isolation operating systems depend on. "Meltdown: Reading Kernel Memory from User Space" (2018) showed an unprivileged process could read protected kernel memory by abusing speculative execution, instantly turning microarchitectural side channels into a first-class OS security problem. Alongside it, 2018 work pushed hard on finding kernel bugs and turning them into exploits — "MoonShine: Optimizing OS Fuzzer Seed Selection with Trace Distillation" (2018) sharpened system-call fuzzing, while "FUZE: Towards Facilitating Exploit Generation for Kernel Use-After-Free Vulnerabilities" (2018) automated the leap from a known bug to a working exploit. The same year broadened the isolation conversation beyond the kernel, with "IMIX: In-Process Memory Isolation EXtension" (2018) and "Security Namespace: Making Linux Security Frameworks Available to Containers" (2018) adapting protection to finer-grained, containerized worlds.

Around 2019-2020 the field shifted toward making isolation both practical and cheap, and toward systematically auditing the kernel's own access-control logic. "ERIM: Secure, Efficient In-process Isolation with Protection Keys (MPK)" (2019) made hardware protection keys a serious building block for splitting a process's secrets from the rest of its code, and "Donky: Domain Keys - Efficient In-Process Isolation for RISC-V and x86" (2020) carried that idea across architectures. At the same time, static-analysis papers like "PeX: A Permission Check Analysis Framework for Linux Kernel" (2019) and "Detecting Missing-Check Bugs via Semantic- and Context-Aware Criticalness and Constraints Inferences" (2019) attacked the problem of missing or wrong permission checks at scale, while fuzzing expanded to the messy device-driver and USB attack surface with "USBFuzz: A Framework for Fuzzing USB Drivers by Device Emulation" (2020) and "Agamotto: Accelerating Kernel Driver Fuzzing with Lightweight Virtual Machine Checkpoints" (2020).

A recurring lesson of this period was that new isolation mechanisms invite new attacks. "PKU Pitfalls: Attacks on PKU-based Memory Isolation Systems" (2020) showed the very protection-key schemes researchers had embraced could be bypassed, and "Jenny: Securing Syscalls for PKU-based Memory Isolation Systems" (2022) responded by hardening the syscall boundary those schemes leak through. Fuzzing kept climbing the stack and getting smarter, moving to hypervisors and learning-guided strategies with "Nyx: Greybox Hypervisor Fuzzing using Fast Snapshots and Affine Types" (2021) and "SyzVegas: Beating Kernel Fuzzing Odds with Reinforcement Learning" (2021).

Most recently the area has come full circle back to the hardware-isolation crisis Meltdown opened, with transient-execution and side-channel attacks growing more refined and harder to mitigate. "AMD Prefetch Attacks through Power and Time" (2022) and especially "Downfall: Exploiting Speculative Data Gathering" (2023) demonstrate that breaking the user-kernel and cross-domain boundary through speculation and data-gathering instructions remains a live, evolving threat. Where the field stands now is a tension between ever-cheaper software and hardware isolation primitives and a steady stream of microarchitectural attacks that erode their guarantees, with automated bug-finding and exploit generation continuing to mature in parallel.</narrative>

milestones.title: Meltdown: Reading Kernel Memory from User Space
milestones.note: redefined OS security by showing speculative execution breaks the kernel/user memory boundary in hardware

milestones.title: MoonShine: Optimizing OS Fuzzer Seed Selection with Trace Distillation
milestones.note: advanced systematic system-call fuzzing as the workhorse for finding kernel vulnerabilities

milestones.title: ERIM: Secure, Efficient In-process Isolation with Protection Keys (MPK)
milestones.note: made hardware protection keys a practical, low-overhead primitive for intra-process isolation

milestones.title: PeX: A Permission Check Analysis Framework for Linux Kernel
milestones.note: brought scalable static analysis to auditing the kernel's own access-control checks

milestones.title: PKU Pitfalls: Attacks on PKU-based Memory Isolation Systems
milestones.note: exposed that the protection-key isolation schemes the field had adopted were themselves attackable

milestones.title: Nyx: Greybox Hypervisor Fuzzing using Fast Snapshots and Affine Types
milestones.note: pushed greybox fuzzing up to the hypervisor isolation boundary with fast snapshotting

milestones.title: Jenny: Securing Syscalls for PKU-based Memory Isolation Systems
milestones.note: hardened the syscall boundary that PKU-based isolation schemes depend on, answering earlier attacks

milestones.title: Downfall: Exploiting Speculative Data Gathering
milestones.note: showed transient-execution attacks on cross-domain isolation remain a refined, live threat years after Meltdown
